observations.finding: Treated fields markedly less confluent than DMSO; cells isolated or in small clusters with large empty background vs DMSO dense cobblestone monolayer.

notable_cells.why: Large cell with multiple DAPI foci and intense green tubulin, irregular nucleus - example of enlarged/multinucleated phenotype.
Cluster with long green tubulin extensions and red spiky actin periphery, stellate morphology vs DMSO.

candidate_mechanisms.why: Combination of increased fraction large nuclei + decreased form factor + decreased DNA mean intensity + cytoskeletal remodeling with high actin/tubulin heterogeneity/contrast and increased eccentricity due to failed cytokinesis/polyploidy. Close differential: strong tub_std z+8.56 and tub_glcm_contrast z+10.6 with bright bundled green tubulin and elongated processes could also indicate direct microtubule stabilization.
Top deviations act_glcm_contrast z+28.9 and act_std z+16.3 with peripheral spiky red actin also consistent with primary actin disruption - considered but less explains marked nuclear enlargement.

observations.finding: Treated fields f_88816922cbd0 and f_61931deea4fa show a largely intact epithelial monolayer, confluence 80-90%. More and larger cell-free gaps (black areas central and left border) than DMSO f_b7ce3f874263 which is >95% confluent. No widespread detachment, debris or pyknotic fragments. Cell number appears modestly reduced, no overt cytotoxicity.

DNA (blue): nuclei remain mostly ovoid, uniform size, no multinucleation, fragmentation, micronuclei or gross enlargement. Nuclei in treated appear slightly paler blue (lower DAPI intensity) than DMSO where nuclei are deeper blue, but shape is preserved, perhaps slightly more round.

Beta-tubulin (green): cytoplasmic network surrounds nuclei in interphase cells, preserved in both treated and DMSO. F-actin (red): cortical/intercellular filament network present in treated and DMSO, no actin puncta, aggregates, loss or retraction. Red signal appears essentially intact, possibly slightly lower contrast/variation in treated (less prominent bright cables) but not disrupted.

second doublet of rounded mitotic cells with condensed chromatin

report.uncertainty: Only composites provided (no separate grayscale DNA/tubulin/actin channels) limits assessment of spindle morphology, DNA texture, and actin filaments. Contrast settings identical to DMSO.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound is bryostatin (PubChem CID 6435419) with ground truth Kinase inhibitors vs our call Actin disruptors p=0.64 - incorrect. The phenotype we measured was real but the inference to a direct actin target was wrong.

What evidence got right:
- The cytoskeletal signal was strong, monotonic and graded, not noise. Well w_63411a268e at 10 uM e2 act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std z=+16.3 and well w_a95f2de41b at 3 uM e8 act_glcm_contrast z=+19.4, act_std +11.9, cell_solidity z=-15.9. Dose response over 4 wells/4 doses was rho=+1.00 p=0 for act_glcm_contrast e11, act_mean e20, act_std e21 and tub_glcm_contrast e12 / tub_std e22. Cell count loss was also monotonic rho=-1.00 p=0 e18, and density lower vs DMSO noted in all describe_phenotype calls e4,e5,e10.
- We correctly excluded a classic Aurora/polyploidy mitotic phenotype despite initial microscopist candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors e4,e10: nuc_dna_mean was decreased not increased (z=-5.2 at 0.1 uM e3, z=-7.8 at 1 uM e7), dose response rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e13, frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 not significant e14, nuc_area rho=-0.63 p=0.37 e17. No corresponding mitotic phenotype as review noted.
- The tubulin co-elevation was captured but treated as secondary correctly in magnitude: tub_glcm_contrast +10.6 e2 at high dose vs actin +29.0.

What misled and why we down-weighted correct signal:
- The extreme actin z-scores and dose-response significance were taken as evidence for a direct actin mechanism. Because bryostatin is a PKC modulator, PKC activation itself remodels actin - this phenocopy was not considered. Literature in this run establishes this link: binding of epi-bryostatin to protein kinase C PMID 2001329, Protein kinase C as kinase target PMID 9147607, and specifically that remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton is coordinately regulated by protein kinase C PMID 9802902, actin-based features negatively regulated by PKC-epsilon PMID 17035302, and phorbol ester-induced cytoskeletal remodeling controlled by PKC scaffolding PMID 21903576. Bryostatin 1 modulation via protein kinase D1 PMID 18765827 also points to kinase, not direct actin, activity. Our search e26 "bryostatin protein kinase C modulator mechanism" returned 42 hits but we did not integrate it before update_hypotheses e19; search e27 for "bryostatin actin" returned 0 hits which falsely reinforced a direct actin read, while e28 "PKC actin cytoskeleton remodeling" returned 53 hits - exactly the explanatory mechanism.
- Microscopist candidates e4 listed Actin disruptors/Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora and e10 narrowed to Actin/Aurora on 4 fields; we used this to support actin e19, overweighting qualitative calls over the atlas.
- We acquired only the upper half of the dose range (0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM from 8 doses 0.003-10 uM e1). This captured the late cytotoxic/cytoskeletal collapse but no low-dose pre-cytoskeletal kinase signaling. Acquisition choice was high-dose maximal phenotype anchor e2+e3, then bridging 1 uM e7 and 3 uM e8, without replicates (4 of 4 wells left but no replicate acquired) to test robustness of the NSC vote.

What we missed:
- compare_to_reference_atlas correctly voted Kinase inhibitors as NSC plurality: 1/2 over 2 wells e6 and 2/4 over 4 wells e9, with k-neighbors split Actin 3/10, Protein degradation 3/10 e6 and then 2/10 each Protein degradation/Actin/DNA replication e9. This was contradicting evidence for actin in e19 but we assigned it only 0.07 to Kinase inhibitors vs 0.64 Actin, explicitly outweighing the atlas prior in update_hypotheses rationale e19.
- lookup_compound e24,e25 returned ChEMBL none curated, which we interpreted as unknown mechanism, when PubChem identity agreement and literature PMID 2001329 should have prompted a PKC-first hypothesis. The dose dependent actin/tubulin texture and decreasing solidity e16 rho=-0.80 are consistent with downstream PKC-driven remodeling, not only barbed-end capping.

In a real lab, the next experiment would need to discriminate direct actin binding from kinase-mediated remodeling, e.g. early timepoint PKC translocation/phospho-PKC-substrate readout at low-dose bryostatin vs phorbol ester control, plus G/F-actin fractionation, rather than phalloidin washout alone.
No clinical implications are inferred from this screening phenotype.

## Reflection

Unblinded compound is bryostatin (PubChem CID 6435419) with ground truth Kinase inhibitors vs our call Actin disruptors p=0.64 - incorrect. The phenotype we measured was real but the inference to a direct actin target was wrong.

What evidence got right:
- The cytoskeletal signal was strong, monotonic and graded, not noise. Well w_63411a268e at 10 uM e2 act_glcm_contrast z=+29.0, act_std z=+16.3 and well w_a95f2de41b at 3 uM e8 act_glcm_contrast z=+19.4, act_std +11.9, cell_solidity z=-15.9. Dose response over 4 wells/4 doses was rho=+1.00 p=0 for act_glcm_contrast e11, act_mean e20, act_std e21 and tub_glcm_contrast e12 / tub_std e22. Cell count loss was also monotonic rho=-1.00 p=0 e18, and density lower vs DMSO noted in all describe_phenotype calls e4,e5,e10.
- We correctly excluded a classic Aurora/polyploidy mitotic phenotype despite initial microscopist candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors e4,e10: nuc_dna_mean was decreased not increased (z=-5.2 at 0.1 uM e3, z=-7.8 at 1 uM e7), dose response rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e13, frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.80 p=0.2 not significant e14, nuc_area rho=-0.63 p=0.37 e17. No corresponding mitotic phenotype as review noted.
- The tubulin co-elevation was captured but treated as secondary correctly in magnitude: tub_glcm_contrast +10.6 e2 at high dose vs actin +29.0.

What misled and why we down-weighted correct signal:
- The extreme actin z-scores and dose-response significance were taken as evidence for a direct actin mechanism. Because bryostatin is a PKC modulator, PKC activation itself remodels actin - this phenocopy was not considered. Literature in this run establishes this link: binding of epi-bryostatin to protein kinase C PMID 2001329, Protein kinase C as kinase target PMID 9147607, and specifically that remodeling of the actin cytoskeleton is coordinately regulated by protein kinase C PMID 9802902, actin-based features negatively regulated by PKC-epsilon PMID 17035302, and phorbol ester-induced cytoskeletal remodeling controlled by PKC scaffolding PMID 21903576. Bryostatin 1 modulation via protein kinase D1 PMID 18765827 also points to kinase, not direct actin, activity. Our search e26 "bryostatin protein kinase C modulator mechanism" returned 42 hits but we did not integrate it before update_hypotheses e19; search e27 for "bryostatin actin" returned 0 hits which falsely reinforced a direct actin read, while e28 "PKC actin cytoskeleton remodeling" returned 53 hits - exactly the explanatory mechanism.
- Microscopist candidates e4 listed Actin disruptors/Microtubule stabilizers/Aurora and e10 narrowed to Actin/Aurora on 4 fields; we used this to support actin e19, overweighting qualitative calls over the atlas.
- We acquired only the upper half of the dose range (0.1, 1, 3, 10 uM from 8 doses 0.003-10 uM e1). This captured the late cytotoxic/cytoskeletal collapse but no low-dose pre-cytoskeletal kinase signaling. Acquisition choice was high-dose maximal phenotype anchor e2+e3, then bridging 1 uM e7 and 3 uM e8, without replicates (4 of 4 wells left but no replicate acquired) to test robustness of the NSC vote.

What we missed:
- compare_to_reference_atlas correctly voted Kinase inhibitors as NSC plurality: 1/2 over 2 wells e6 and 2/4 over 4 wells e9, with k-neighbors split Actin 3/10, Protein degradation 3/10 e6 and then 2/10 each Protein degradation/Actin/DNA replication e9. This was contradicting evidence for actin in e19 but we assigned it only 0.07 to Kinase inhibitors vs 0.64 Actin, explicitly outweighing the atlas prior in update_hypotheses rationale e19.
- lookup_compound e24,e25 returned ChEMBL none curated, which we interpreted as unknown mechanism, when PubChem identity agreement and literature PMID 2001329 should have prompted a PKC-first hypothesis. The dose dependent actin/tubulin texture and decreasing solidity e16 rho=-0.80 are consistent with downstream PKC-driven remodeling, not only barbed-end capping.

In a real lab, the next experiment would need to discriminate direct actin binding from kinase-mediated remodeling, e.g. early timepoint PKC translocation/phospho-PKC-substrate readout at low-dose bryostatin vs phorbol ester control, plus G/F-actin fractionation, rather than phalloidin washout alone.
No clinical implications are inferred from this screening phenotype.

What was right:
- act_glcm_contrast +29.0 and act_std +16.3 at 10 uM e2 and +19.4 at 3 uM e8 with monotonic rho=+1.00 p=0 e11,e20,e21 were real cytoskeletal changes
- correctly noted lack of polyploidy/DNA increase: nuc_dna_mean -5.2 e3 and -7.8 e7, rho -0.80 p=0.2 e13, nuc_area rho -0.63 p0.37 e17
- tubulin co-elevation rho=+1.00 p0 e12 positive but lower magnitude +10.6 e2 was recorded

What was wrong or missed:
- treated extreme actin texture and cell_solidity -15.9 e8 as direct actin disruptor despite literature that PKC regulates actin remodeling PMID 9802902 PMID 17035302 PMID 21903576 and bryostatin binds PKC PMID 2001329
- down-weighted NSC vote Kinase inhibitors 1/2 e6 and 2/4 e9 to 0.07 in e19 vs Actin 0.64
- followed microscopist candidates Actin e4 e10 over atlas split, sampling only 0.1-10 uM without low-dose 0.003-0.03 uM or replicates

Proposed next experiment: Early time course (15 min-2h) at low doses 0.01-0.3 uM: PKC membrane translocation / pan-phospho-PKC substrate western +/- PKC inhibitor (e.g. Go6983) to test if actin texture changes e11 and solidity e16 are blocked, plus direct actin biochemistry vs cytochalasin D control
